source.title: CBSE Sample Question Paper, Mathematics Standard (041), Class X, 2025-26
source.subject: mathematics
source.usage: Official CBSE publication, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: This is the CBSE Sample Question Paper (SQP) for the 2025-26 academic session, examined in the year 2026 board exams (examYear=2026). It is not tied to a specific past board exam; there is no Q.P./set code printed (only the fixed subject code 041, included in paperName). 38 questions, 8 printed pages, Maximum Marks 80, Time 3 hours; English-medium only (no Hindi text observed in the extraction). The paper prints a 'For Visually Impaired candidates' alternative question for Q7, Q24(A), Q26, Q31, and for the whole of Q37 (replacing the case study's figure with the coordinates as text); these alternatives were intentionally NOT imported into this pack, per instructions. The marking scheme (MathsStandard-MS.pdf, 12 pages) lost a large amount of fraction/equation content during text extraction (numerators, denominators and some full derivation lines are blank in the text layer even though pdftotext parsed the page); every officialAnswer built from an incomplete scheme line is flagged with 'Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation)'. Where the underlying numeric value could still be derived unambiguously (matching the scheme's stated final answer), it is included and flagged as notation rebuilt from the PDF layout. The source PDF's text layer frequently splits fractions/powers across lines and renders variables as math italic Unicode (e.g. x, theta); such notation is rebuilt to plain-text form (x, /, ^, theta) only where the layout makes it unambiguous (flagged MEDIUM), otherwise left as extracted and flagged LOW. Two tables (Q35(A) frequency distribution, Q35(B) cumulative-frequency heights) were extracted with column values out of row order and were reconstructed positionally, cross-checked against the marking scheme's own working.

questions.text: If AP and DQ are medians of triangles ABC and DEF respectively, where ∆ABC~ ∆DEF, then prove that AB/DE = AP/DQ
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.
Math italic Unicode letters normalised to plain text (e.g. 𝑥→x, ϑ→θ).
Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation).

officialAnswer.text:
△ABC~△DEF
⇒ AB/DE = BC/EF
AB/DE = 2B/2EQ (AP and DQ are the medians)
AB/DE = BP/EQ
In △ABP and △DEQ
AB/DE = BP/EQ
∠B=∠E (△ABC~△DEF)
⇒△ABP ~△DEQ
Hence, AB/DE = AP/DQ

questions.text: A horse, a cow and a goat are tied, each by ropes of length 14m, at the corners A, B and C respectively, of a grassy triangular field ABC with sides of lengths 35m, 40m and 50 m. Find the area of grass field that can be grazed by them.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text: Area grazed = (θA+θB+θC)/360 × πr², where θA+θB+θC=180° (angle sum of the triangle) and r=14m: = (180/360)×π×14² = 98π = 308 m².

questions.text: Find the area of the major segment (in terms of π) of a circle of radius 5cm, formed by a chord subtending an angle of 90˚ at the centre.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.
Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation).

officialAnswer.text: Area of minor segment = area of sector − area of triangle = (90/360)π(5)² − (1/2)(5)(5) = (25π/4 − 25/2) cm². Area of major segment = area of circle − area of minor segment = 25π − (25π/4 − 25/2) = (75π/4 + 25/2) cm².

questions.text: A ∆ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that the segments BD and DC are of lengths 10 cm and 8 cm respectively. Find the lengths of the sides AB and AC, if it is given that ar(∆ABC) = 90cm²
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text:
Let r be the radius of the inscribed circle
BD=BE=10cm
CD=CF=8cm
Let AF=AE= x
ar(△ABC) =ar(△AOC) + ar(△BOC) + ar(△AOB)
=½ × r x AC + ½ × r × BC +½ × r × AB
90 = ½ × 4 (x +8+18+ x +10)
x = 4.5cm
∴ AB=4.5+10=14.5cm
AC=4.5+8=12.5cm

extractionIssues: Figure on page 5 (circle with parallel tangents XY, X′Y′ and tangent AB touching at C) not reproduced.

officialAnswer.text: In ∆APO and ∆ACO: AP=AC (tangents from an external point), AO=AO (common), OP=OC (radii), so ∆APO≅∆ACO. Similarly ∆BQO≅∆BCO. ∠POQ=180° (PQ is a diameter). ∠POA+∠COA+∠QOB+∠COB=180°, i.e. 2∠COA+2∠COB=180°, so ∠COA+∠COB=90°, i.e. ∠AOB=90°.

questions.text: If sinθ + cosθ = √3, then prove that tanθ + cotθ = 1
extractionIssues: Math italic Unicode letters normalised to plain text (e.g. 𝑥→x, ϑ→θ).

officialAnswer.text: sinθ+cosθ=√3 ⇒ (sinθ+cosθ)²=3 ⇒ 1+2sinθcosθ=3 ⇒ 2sinθcosθ=2 ⇒ sinθcosθ=1. So tanθ+cotθ = sinθ/cosθ + cosθ/sinθ = (sin²θ+cos²θ)/(sinθcosθ) = 1/1 = 1.

questions.text:
On a particular day, Vidhi and Unnati couldn’t decide on who would get to drive the car. They had one coin each and flipped their coin exactly three times. The following was agreed upon:
1. If Vidhi gets two heads in a row, she would drive the car
2. If Unnati gets a head immediately followed by a tail, she would drive the car.
Who has greater probability to drive the car that day? Justify your answer.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text: P(Vidhi drives the car) = 3/8, as favourable outcomes are HHT, THH, HHH. P(Unnati drives the car) = 4/8, as favourable outcomes are THT, THH, HTH, TTH. As 4/8 > 3/8, Unnati has greater probability to drive the car.

questions.text: The monthly income of Aryan and Babban are in the ratio 3:4 and their monthly expenditures are in ratio 5:7. If each saves ₹ 15,000 per month, find their monthly incomes.
extractionIssues: Math italic Unicode letters normalised to plain text (e.g. 𝑥→x, ϑ→θ).

officialAnswer.text: Let incomes be 3x and 4x, expenditures 5y and 7y. 3x−5y=15000 and 4x−7y=15000. Solving, x=30000, so incomes are ₹90,000 and ₹1,20,000 respectively.

Solve the following system of equations graphically:
2x + y =6, 2x – y – 2=0. Find the area of the triangle so formed by two lines and x-axis.
extractionIssues: Math italic Unicode letters normalised to plain text (e.g. 𝑥→x, ϑ→θ).

officialAnswer.text: Solving graphically, the solution is x=2, y=2. Area of the triangle formed by the two lines and the x-axis = 2 sq. units.

questions.text: A train travels at a certain average speed for a distance of 63km and then travels at a distance of 72km at an average speed of 6km/hr more than its original speed. If it takes 3 hours to complete the total journey, what is the original average speed?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text: Let original speed be x km/hr. 63/x + 72/(x+6) = 3. This gives 63(x+6)+72x = 3(x+6)x ⇒ 135x+378 = 3x²+18x ⇒ 3x²−117x−378=0 ⇒ x²−39x−126=0 ⇒ x²−42x+3x−126=0 ⇒ (x+3)(x−42)=0. As x can't be negative, x=42 km/hr.

questions.text:
Prove that if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the sameratio.
Hence in ΔPQR, prove that a line ℓ intersects the sides PQ and PR of a ∆PQR at L and M respectively such that LM II QR. If PL = 5.7cm, PQ=15.2cm and MR=5.5cm, then find the length of PM (in cm)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.
Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation).

officialAnswer.text: Correct given, figure and construction; correct proof (Basic Proportionality Theorem). Since LM∥QR, PL/LQ = PM/MR. LQ = PQ−PL = 15.2−5.7 = 9.5cm. PM = (PL×MR)/LQ = (5.7×5.5)/9.5 = 3.3cm.

questions.text: From a solid right circular cone, whose height is 6cm and radius of base is 12cm, a right circular cylindrical cavity of height 3cm and radius 4cm is hollowed out such that bases of cone and cylinder form concentric circles. Find the surface area of the remaining solid in terms of π.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.
Math italic Unicode letters normalised to plain text (e.g. 𝑥→x, ϑ→θ).

officialAnswer.text: Slant height L=√(R²+H²)=√(12²+6²)=3√20 cm. Curved surface area of cone=πRL=π×12×3√20=(36√20)π cm². Area of exposed base circle of cone (outer − cylinder cross-section, plus top of cylinder)=πR²=144π cm². Curved surface area of cylinder=2πrh=2π×4×3=24π cm². Surface area of remaining solid = 36√20π+144π+24π = (168+36√20)π cm².

questions.text: An empty cone of radius 3cm and height 12cm is filled with ice-cream such that the lower part of the cone which is (1/6)th of the volume of the cone is unfilled (empty) but a hemisphere is formed on the top. Find the volume of the ice-cream.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text: Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π×3×3×12 = 36πcm³. Volume of ice-cream in the cone = (5/6)×36π = 30π cm³. Volume of ice-cream in the hemispherical part = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π×3×3×3 = 18π cm³. Total volume of ice-cream = 30π+18π = 48π ≈ 150.86 cm³ (approx.).

questions.text:
In a class, the teacher asks every student to write an example of A.P. Two boys Aryan and Roshan writes the progression as −5, −2,1,4, …… and 187, 184, 181, …. respectively. Now the teacher asks his various students the following questions on progression.

Help the students to find answers for the following:

(i) Find the sum of the common difference of two progressions. (1)
(ii) Find the 34th term of progression written by Roshan. (1)
(iii) (A) Find the sum of first 10 terms of the progression written by Aryan. (2)
OR
(iii) (B) Which term of the progressions will have the same value? (2)
extractionIssues: Sub-part marks shown in brackets were printed in the margin.
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Common difference of Aryan's A.P. = 3; of Roshan's A.P. = −3. Sum = 0.
(ii) t34 (Roshan) = 187+(34−1)(−3) = 88.
(iii)(A) Sum of first 10 terms (Aryan) = (10/2)[2(−5)+(10−1)(3)] = 85.
OR
(iii)(B) −5+(n−1)3 = 187+(n−1)(−3) gives n = 33.

questions.text:
A group of class X students goes to picnic during winter holidays. The position of three friends Aman, Kirti and Chahat are shown by the points P, Q and R

(i) Find the distance between P and R. (1)
(ii) Is Q, the midpoint of PR? Justify by finding midpoint of PR. (1)
(iii) (A) Find the point on x-axis which is equidistant from P and Q. (2)
OR
(iii) (B) Let S be a point which divides the line joining PQ in ratio 2:3. Find the coordinates of S. (2)
extractionIssues: Sub-part marks shown in brackets were printed in the margin.
Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation).

officialAnswer.text:
(i) PR = √[(8 − 2)² + (3 − 5)²] = 2√10
(ii) Co-ordinates of Q (4,4).
The mid-point of PR is (5,4)
∴Q is not the mid-point of PR
(iii) (A) Let the point be (x,0)
So, √[(2 − x)² + 25] = √[(4 − x)² + 16]
Hence x = 3/4. Therefore the point is (3/4,0).
OR
(B) The coordinates of S will be
((2×4+3×2)/(2+3), (2×4+3×5)/(2+3))
= (14/5, 23/5)

questions.text:
India gate (formerly known as All India war memorial) is located near Karthavya path. (formerly Rajpath) at New Delhi. It stands as a memorial to 74187 soldiers of Indian Army, who gave their life in the first world war. This 42m tall structure was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens in the style of Roman triumphal arches. A student Shreya of height 1 m visited India Gate as a part of her study tour.

(i) What is the angle of elevation from Shreya’s eye to the top of India Gate, if she is standing at a distance of 41m away from the India Gate? (1)
(ii) If Shreya observes the angle of elevation from her eye to the top of India Gate to be 60ᵒ, then how far is the she standing from the base of the India Gate? (1)
(iii) (A) If the angle of elevation from Shreya’s eye changes from 45° to 30°, when she moves some distance back from the original position. Find the distance she moves back. (2)
OR
(iii) (B) If Shreya moves to a point which is at a distance of 41/√3 m from the India Gate, then find the angle of elevation made by her eye to the top of India Gate. (2)
